description.narrative: The draft power sector master plan 2010, updated 2016, identifies the need to add 11 CCPPs each with 450 MW capacity by 2016. The proposed Ashuganj 450 MW plant (part A) can be considered one of these CCPPs. Further, the government has identified the proposed plant as a priority project in its expansion plan. The economic cost of electricity supply from the Ashuganj CCPP is similar to or lower than those of a coal-fired power plant (based on the costs taken from the master plan), confirming that the proposed plant is among the least-cost options for generating new capacity. CCPP design will use the latest commercially available technology to harness the maximum benefit of energy efficiency. Part B of the project will demonstrate renewable energy technologies and their application for long-term large-scale penetration into the Bangladesh power system. The sub components in part B use solar photovoltaic, wind power and LEDs, which are commercially proven technologies. Additional financing will be utilized for installation of 2,000 solar irrigation pumps in ten different districts of Bangladesh.

description.narrative: Increased electricity generating capacity

Total installed generation capacity increased to 5,909 MW by 2016 (2011 baseline: installed generation capacity of 5,719MW) Achievement: 0 Progress/Status: Part A: Output achieved. Construction of Ashuganj 450 MW CCPP(North) is commissioned on 11 June 2017; has been operational since.
Part B(i)- Output achieved. Kaptai 7.4 MW Solar Power Plant was commissioned on 6 May 2019; has been operational since.
Part B(ii)-Hatiya: Output cancelled. Hatiya solar-diesel hybrid power generation component was cancelled by the request of the borrower in 2016.
Part B(iii)-Solar Street Light: Output achieved. 8 contracts for streetlights were signed on 26 April 2017. Installation and commissioning of LED streetlights in 7 city corporations completed on 31 March 2019. Dhaka North City Corporation (the 8th City Corporation) cancelled the component. The cancellation has been reflected in the project by the request of the borrower in 2018.
Part B(iv)-Solar Irrigation Component. The output was added to the project through a scope change (comprising reallocation of $20 million loan proceeds to BREB) approved by ADB in 2016. Additional Financing of $25.224 million grant proceeds (Grant 0582/83-BAN) was approved on 5 July 2018, to match the reallocated loan proceeds of $20 million. Project implementation activities initiated from 2018. BREB awarded one consultancy contract for design and implementation supervision on 31 January 2019; one consultancy contract for the project's GAP implementation on 30 Sep 2019; two EPC contracts for 705 solar irrigation pumps on 16 Nov 2020 and four EPC contracts for 1295 solar irrigation pumps on 26 May 2021. One contract was signed on 29 Dec 2024 to connect 1295 number of solar irrigation pump with the electricity grid. Till date, 610 units of solar irrigation pumps have been installed (30.5%). Data Source: Annual reports of APSC, BPDB, and Power Division
